biography: Rodrigo Helal, a name synonymous with flair and daring in the Brazilian Opala Old Stock Race, hails from the vibrant streets of São Paulo. His racing journey began not on the polished asphalt of a professional track, but on the dusty dirt roads of his family's fazenda, where he honed his car control skills drifting a beat-up old pickup. He entered the Opala Old Stock Race scene with a bang, immediately captivating the crowd with his aggressive driving style and flamboyant personality. While early seasons were marked by spectacular crashes and near misses, Rodrigo matured, learning to balance risk with calculated precision. Now in his early thirties, Rodrigo is considered to be at the height of his powers, a seasoned competitor with a hunger for victory and an unyielding desire to entertain.
drivingStyle: Rodrigo's driving style is best described as 'controlled chaos.' He's known for his late braking maneuvers, often diving into corners with reckless abandon, somehow managing to find the grip needed to power out. While his aggressive approach can lead to mistakes, it also makes him incredibly difficult to overtake. He is particularly adept at managing tire wear, a crucial skill in the demanding Opala Old Stock Race, often conserving his tires early in a race before unleashing his full pace in the final laps. He thrives under pressure, often pulling off stunning overtakes when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from Ricardo's criticisms of Rodrigo's 'unsportsmanlike' driving. The two have traded paint (and words) on numerous occasions.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of bright yellow socks under his racing suit.
Listens to a specific 80s rock anthem on repeat for 30 minutes before every race.
Refuses to enter his car from the right side, always entering from the left.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about winning; it's about putting on a show. If I can't win, I'll at least make sure everyone remembers my name!"
careerHighlight: Winning the 2021 Opala Old Stock Race Championship after a season-long battle, culminating in a nail-biting final race where he overtook his rival on the last lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at Interlagos in 2019, a race he was widely expected to win, due to a mechanical failure caused by his own overly aggressive driving.
